# Overview

## What this repository is

A three-file Terraform root configuration (kind: `iac`, `docs/architecture/_run/classify.json` evidence: `*.tf present`). There is no README, no CI config, no tests, no variables, and no state backend anywhere in the checkout.

## Context

The root configuration (`main.tf`) is applied by a human operator running the Terraform CLI. It talks to two things:
- **AWS**, via the `aws` provider (`main.tf:1-8` pins `hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0`; `main.tf:10-12` sets `region = "us-east-1"`) — every resource in the tree is `aws_*`.
- **The local workspace**, because no `backend` block is declared, so Terraform state defaults to a local `terraform.tfstate` file.

No other system is evidenced: there is no git remote configured (`git remote -v` returns nothing) and no `.github/workflows`, so the seeded template edges to GitHub and to a log store were removed from `docs/architecture/model/hand.c4` rather than kept unevidenced. Rendered PNGs for this context/container view could not be produced this run — see [Gaps](#gaps-and-limitations).

## Module call graph

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  root["root (main.tf)"] --> network["module.network\n(./modules/network)"]
  root --> app["module.app\n(./modules/app)"]
```

`root` calls both child modules (`main.tf:14-20`). Neither module declares an input variable or an output, and the root module passes no value between them, so **`app` and `network` are not wired to each other** — this is also flagged in `docs/architecture/risks.md`, row 1. Full detail: `docs/reference/infra.md`.

## Providers

| name | version | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| aws | ~> 5.0 | `main.tf:3-6` |

Exactly one provider is declared and used. `docs/reference/deps.md` also lists `aws` as `unused` — that is a false positive of the dependency extractor, not a real finding; see [Gaps](#gaps-and-limitations).

## Resource inventory

| type | name | module | file |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| aws_vpc | main | network | `modules/network/main.tf:1-3` |
| aws_instance | web | app | `modules/app/main.tf:1-4` |
| aws_instance | worker | app | `modules/app/main.tf:6-9` |

3 resources, 2 types, across 2 modules. Full detail: `docs/reference/infra.md`.

## What the config does not declare

Confirmed absent by directly reading the tree, not inferred: `variables.tf`/input variables, `outputs.tf`/outputs, a `backend` block, a `required_version` constraint, resource `tags`, `.tfvars` files, a `.gitignore`, CI/CD config (`.github/workflows` or equivalent), a test suite, and lint/policy config (`.tflint.hcl`, checkov, etc.).

## Gaps and limitations

See `docs/architecture/_run/kit-issues.md` (tooling limitations), `docs/architecture/_run/review.md` (project-facing findings), and `docs/architecture/_run/interview.md` (open questions for a human). Summary:
- The rendered C4 PNGs (context/container/component views) could not be produced this run: LikeC4 rendering needs `npx`, which needs network access to `registry.npmjs.org`, and that host was denied by the sandbox. `docs/architecture/model/hand.c4` and `generated.c4` are the source of truth for the views the images would have shown.
- `docs/reference/components.md` shows 0 components/edges. The kit's import-graph engines (`builtin`, `go`, `dependency-cruiser`) parse source-code imports; none of them parse HCL/Terraform module blocks, so the module call graph is only captured in `docs/reference/infra.md`, not `components.md`.
- `docs/reference/deps.md` marks the `aws` provider `unused` because the dependency extractor looks for an import-style usage site; it has no notion that a Terraform provider is used implicitly by every `aws_*` resource block. Treat that row as a known false positive, not a real orphaned dependency.
- Whether `ami-123456` (`modules/app/main.tf:2,7`) is a valid AMI in the target account/region cannot be determined from the code — it is shorter than a real AWS AMI id.
- Which credential source (env vars, shared config file, instance profile, SSO) is used when `terraform apply` runs cannot be determined from the code — the `aws` provider block sets only `region`.
- Whether the account default VPC (rather than `aws_vpc.main`) receiving the two instances is intentional or an oversight cannot be determined from the code.
